reply_text:
㊥ Gist: Yes, your guess holds. Comparing hits before and after 21 September, assurance rose from 23.9% to 26.5%, and most of the rise comes from three families: `test-registry`, which went from 0.7% to 3.6% of all hits, then `translation` and `contracts`. Coordination fell from 13.6% to 10.7%, mostly because `orchestration` was retrieved half as often. The shift still holds when the 97 new labels are left out, with assurance at 26.2%, so it doesn't depend on the Kimi readings.

㊢ (families, 22 Aug–21 Sep vs 21 Sep–1 Oct, share of each window's hits)

| family | before | after | stage mix of its hits |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| problems | 9.6% | 10.8% | believe 85, assurance 77, select 64 |
| futon-theory | 4.9 | 5.8 | coordination 73, perceive 37, select 37 |
| test-registry | 1.1 | **4.2** | assurance 64 |
| iching | 3.9 | 4.2 | act 98, select 31 |
| musn | 3.1 | 3.5 | select 59, assurance 39 |
| war-room | 5.6 | 3.1 | select 66, believe 59, perceive 35 |
| cascade-construction | 0.9 | **3.0** | believe 24, assurance 22 |
| devmap-coherence | 4.1 | 2.9 | assurance 135 |
| memory | 4.9 | 2.7 | assurance 108, evaluate 49 |
| inbox-zero | 1.0 | 2.3 | act 40 |
| orchestration | 3.0 | **1.4** | coordination 97 |
| aif | 1.8 | **0.7** | evaluate 23, perceive 16 |

There are 108 families in all. Four appear only after 21 September: `hygiene`, `pattern-mining`, `象` and `corps`.

🖖 (two kinds of assurance) The assurance has changed character. Before 21 September it came from `devmap-coherence`, `memory` and `stack-coherence`, which concern whether the system's own records and maps are consistent with each other. Since then it comes from `test-registry` (warrants, adequacy, reruns), `translation` (testing a port by reproducing behaviour) and `contracts`. That fits War Machine work that has moved from building the records to testing what runs.

㊟ (how far this goes)
- **Topic, not act:** these are retrieval counts. They show what your turns were about, as the search engine matched them, not what each turn did. The PBASE comparison found the two hardly agree.
- **Short window:** the post-21 September window has 1,180 hits over ten days. Families with fewer than about 20 hits there could easily move by chance.
- **Family mixes span both windows:** the stage-mix column pools all hits, so a family's mix can't show a change inside that family.

㭭 (if you want it kept) I'd add this as a "families" section to `PATTERN-STAGES-2026-10-01.md`, built by a short committed script. Each family would get its stage mix in each window, and the list of patterns that changed. A per-family version of the figure is also possible, as small multiples, but the table may be enough. Reply `table` or `figure`, or leave it here.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what its gaps measure: three differences from the Minard panel)
- **Source of your turns:** it finds your typed turns in the agents' own transcripts, not in futon1b. A relayed turn counts as yours only if its header says `Origin: operator`.
- **Early wake-ups split gaps:** before 27 September, park wake-ups were delivered with `From: joe / Origin: operator` headers. That's the 330 I filtered out of the backfill. The reader will count those as typed turns, so some overnight gaps before the 27th will be split or will vanish. That biases toward finding fewer and shorter gaps in that period, not more.
- **Which agents' tokens:** they come from Claude and Codex logs, including cached input. Kimi and Zai work, such as today's overnight loops, runs through Agency rather than those logs and won't appear.
